pk.context: 400 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Bioavailability is over 90%, and food does not affect exposure. Protein binding is low, at 11-12%, and about 80% of the dose leaves the body unchanged in urine.
clues.substance: The active moiety has a molecular weight of 306.27. It is a crystalline solid that is slightly soluble in water and saline.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as tablets of 50, 100, 150 and 200 mg and as a powder for oral suspension, dosed once daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients, and with QT-prolonging CYP3A4 substrates such as erythromycin, pimozide and quinidine.
clues.indication: Vaginal, oropharyngeal and esophageal candidiasis, cryptococcal meningitis, and prevention of candidiasis after bone marrow transplantation.
clues.mechanism: A highly selective inhibitor of fungal lanosterol 14-α-demethylase, which converts lanosterol to ergosterol. Mammalian cells are much less sensitive.

tell: A 1990 triazole antifungal that is over 90% bioavailable and cleared mostly unchanged in urine.

evidence.pk.halfLifeH: terminal plasma elimination half-life of approximately 30 hours
evidence.pk.cmax: administration of a single oral 400 mg dose of DIFLUCAN (fluconazole) leads to a mean C max of 6.72 mcg/mL
evidence.pill: Pink trapezoidal tablets containing 50, 100, or 200 mg
